resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record counts the 1901 tower as Tower 8. The NRHP form counts it as the tenth light including beacons (cite 2), LighthouseFriends as the ninth (cite 4), and Putnam's list gives seven successive lighthouses to 1901 (cite 6). The differences come from whether beacons and range lights are counted.
The record's conflict note is resolved: the USLHS record lists the station as an active aid to navigation, and the 1981 NRHP form lists the station as 'Unmanned/Active'.
The record's 15.5 m does not match the sources. USLHS gives the light 26 ft above mean high water (7.9 m), and the NRHP form and the Bulletin describe a 26-ft tower.
The record says 'deactivated' for 1900 (Rowlett). The Light-House Board's 1900 report describes a new fixed red light 600 feet away while the fourth-order light remained.
LighthouseFriends dates the tower apron to 1923. The Bulletin of 1925 dates the riprap to September 1924 at about $1,500.
The USLHS roster gives Gerald M. Reed from 1927; LighthouseFriends says he was in charge from 1926. The story uses the roster's dates for the list and LighthouseFriends's date in the text.
The NRHP form's description says the Maddaket equipment building was floated to Brant Point in 1934, while its chronology dates the move to 1950. The story omits this building for that reason.
The 1856 tower carried a fourth-order lens (NRHP, LighthouseFriends, Light-House Board 1895). The 1901 tower carries a fifth-order lens (USLHS, Bulletin 1939).

The 1939 Bulletin says the federal government took over in 1789 and that there was then no lighthouse on the point, only possibly a temporary erection. Putnam (6) and the NRHP form (2) date the cession by the Commonwealth to 1795 (the grant of 23 June 1795). The story states both.

The NRHP form (2), Putnam (6) and the 1900 Light-House Board report (8) place the light on the west side of the entrance to Nantucket Harbor; LighthouseFriends (4) says the south side. The story uses west, with the sources named in the footnote.

The Bulletin (3) says Congress appropriated $1,600 for a keeper's residence with a tower and lantern, and LighthouseFriends (4) dates the appropriation to 3 March 1825. The story gives the appropriation date from LighthouseFriends and does not repeat a construction year.

Putnam (6) says the town built the light 'in supposition' that shipping would maintain it but that the town paid the expenses until 1774; the NRHP form (2) gives the six-shilling vessel charge from 1774. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-22 (Haiku). Roster matched by roster.py (name and position, 0.11 km); USLHS roster lines checked against the cached page. Sources read: NRHP form (2) text; LighthouseFriends (4); the Light-House Board reports for 1895, 1900 and 1901 (scan p. 101, 60, 31, all confirmed by corpus.py page); Putnam (scan p. 49, confirmed); the Commissioner's 1920 report (scan 542, printed 44, confirmed) and estimates (scan 688, printed 83, confirmed); the 1921 report's new-construction entry (scan 742, placed in the fiscal year ended June 30, 1921, because the volume's 1921 report starts at scan 603 and no 1922 report is in it); Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1919 (p. 50), 1925 (p. 50), 1926 (p. 19), 1939 (March issue, PDF pp. 13-15; the 1939 OCR is double-column and interleaved, so quotations were checked against the readable lines). The 1888 Coskata station report: printed p. 88 (footer), read in OCR. The 1939 Bulletin's 'some temporary erection' is on PDF p. 15 and the 1774 newspaper item on PDF p. 13. Conflicts stated in the story: 1789 vs 1795 for the federal takeover; west (NRHP, Putnam, LH 1900) vs south (LighthouseFriends) side; the count of lights (NRHP tenth, LighthouseFriends ninth, Putnam seven). The 1888 Onicard grounding is cited to the Coskata report (scan p. 94 via archive.org) and is in OCR. The 1907 newspaper account of the Howes family is cited through LighthouseFriends and was not read. The 1887 Mary E. Coffin dispute is cited through LighthouseFriends and was not read. The 1928 Reed account is printed by LighthouseFriends, not read in the original. The NRHP form's 1981 status line is 'Unmanned/Active'; the USLHS record lists the station as an active aid to navigation. Post-1960 names: none are named in the prose. The roster's 1963 keepers are not in the story. Caution: the 1854 NRHP lantern quotation is OCR'd as 'appratus' in the form; the story quotes only the words after it. The Bulletin's 1939 date and the story's 'March 1939' issue date are confirmed from the issue header.
